name: Sam Bankman-Fried

summary.text: Sam Bankman-Fried founded the cryptocurrency exchange FTX and the trading firm Alameda Research. He was indicted in the Southern District of New York in December 2022 on fraud, money laundering and campaign finance charges, convicted by a jury on seven counts in November 2023 after a one-month trial before Judge Lewis A. Kaplan, and sentenced on March 28, 2024 to 25 years in prison, three years of supervised release and more than $11 billion in forfeiture. Former FTX executive Ryan Salame pleaded guilty in 2023 to conspiring with Bankman-Fried to make unlawful political contributions in the names of straw donors using money that originated in Alameda bank accounts holding FTX customer funds.

facts.claim: On March 28, 2024 Judge Lewis A. Kaplan sentenced Bankman-Fried to 25 years in prison, three years of supervised release and more than $11 billion in forfeiture, after a jury convicted him following a one-month trial. The U.S. Attorney's Office said he defrauded FTX investors of more than $1.7 billion and Alameda's lenders of more than $1.3 billion, and authorized recovered forfeiture funds to compensate victims.
facts.quote: defrauded investors in FTX of more than $1.7 billion, and defrauded lenders to Alameda of more than $1.3 billion

facts.claim: Prosecutors said Bankman-Fried directed co-conspirators to alter FTX's computer code so that Alameda could withdraw effectively unlimited amounts of cryptocurrency from the exchange, and backdated contracts and other documents to conceal his conduct.
facts.quote: directed co-conspirators to alter FTX's computer code to allow Alameda to withdraw effectively unlimited amounts of cryptocurrency from the exchange

facts.claim: NPR reported that Bankman-Fried had been convicted of seven fraud counts, that prosecutors had sought a sentence of 40 to 50 years, and that Judge Kaplan cited his lack of remorse and said he had given false testimony on at least three occasions.
facts.quote: will be in a position to do something very bad in the future, and it's not a trivial risk

facts.claim: Ryan Salame, former co-CEO of FTX Digital Markets, pleaded guilty to conspiracy to make unlawful political contributions and defraud the Federal Election Commission, and to conspiracy to operate an unlicensed money transmitting business. The U.S. Attorney said Bankman-Fried did not want his name publicly attached to Republican candidates and conspired with others to make contributions in the names of Salame and Nishad Singh.
facts.quote: Bankman-Fried, however, did not want to be known as a left-leaning partisan, or to have his name publicly attached to Republican candidates. In order to obscure his association with certain contributions, Bankman-Fried conspired with others

facts.claim: Prosecutors said the political donations originated from Alameda bank accounts, including funds deposited by FTX customers, and amounted to more than 300 contributions totaling tens of millions of dollars that were unlawful because they were made through straw donors or paid with corporate funds. Salame was later sentenced to 90 months in prison, three years of supervised release, more than $6 million in forfeiture and more than $5 million in restitution.
facts.quote: The money used to make these political donations originated from Alameda bank accounts, and included funds that had been deposited by FTX customers.

openQuestions: Site claim (Crash Conduits): political campaigns and PACs received over $100M in donations. The DOJ statement on Salame's plea describes more than 300 contributions totaling tens of millions of dollars; the $100M figure was not confirmed in these sources.

Site claim (Post-Human Resources): the FTX Future Fund made about $130M in grants and investments for longtermist causes in 2022. No source for the $130M figure was found; the fund's team resignation is recorded in research/findings/ftx.json.
Site claim: over 1 million retail customers lost $8+ billion. NPR reported at least $8 billion in customer funds was believed stolen; the customer count was not confirmed.
Site claim that Deltec Bank and Silvergate/Signature cleared FTX flows, and that the collapse paved the way for spot ETF approvals, were not tested here.
The exact date of Salame's guilty plea (the statement is dated September 7, 2023) and the date of his sentencing should be checked against the docket.
